---
title: "Build lagged angles"
description: "Create angular predictors from previous observations within each subject."
---

Use `autoregressivedata()` to add lagged response angles. The function
follows row order within each subject, so sort by time first.

```{r}
library(CircularRegression)

tracks <- data.frame(
  animal = rep(c("A", "B"), each = 3),
  time = rep(1:3, 2),
  direction = c(0.2, 0.3, 0.5, -0.3, -0.1, 0.2)
)
tracks <- tracks[order(tracks$animal, tracks$time), ]
lagged <- autoregressivedata(tracks, response = "direction", p = 2, ID = "animal")
lagged
```

The first row for each animal has no first lag. The first two rows have
no second lag. Each lag refers to an earlier recorded observation.
Account for the observation intervals when interpreting a lag from an
irregular track.
